questions.q: The editorial calls social media potentially “a study club.” What decides whether it turns out so for a given person?
options: The country he lives in
Not quite. The article says: The choice he makes – to use it to learn from others, or to spread complaints and unverified news.
The device he uses
Not quite. The article says: The choice he makes – to use it to learn from others, or to spread complaints and unverified news.
The number of friends he has on it
Not quite. The article says: The choice he makes – to use it to learn from others, or to spread complaints and unverified news.
The choice he makes – to use it to learn from others, or to spread complaints and unverified news
Yes. Everything can be used either way.
questions.rationale: “Everything in this world could be used to develop oneself positively or can be used to spread negativity. One should make responsible choices.”

questions.q: People asked which name of God to recite for protection in the pandemic. How does the article say the names of God should be understood?
options: As words whose power lies in their sound
Not quite. The article says: Not as mysterious formulas to chant, but as attributes to understand and call on with meaning.
As charms to be written and worn
Not quite. The article says: Not as mysterious formulas to chant, but as attributes to understand and call on with meaning.
Not as mysterious formulas to chant, but as attributes to understand and call on with meaning
Right. “Known doors of God’s mercy.”
As secrets known only to a few
Not quite. The article says: Not as mysterious formulas to chant, but as attributes to understand and call on with meaning.
questions.rationale: “It is not about chanting, it is about understanding and discovering the attribute and beseeching God to help us in a particular situation.”

questions.q: According to the Hadith quoted, what is supplication – calling upon God?
options: A duty of scholars on behalf of others
Not quite. The article says: The kernel of worship, and something each person must do for himself.
A lesser form of worship
Not quite. The article says: The kernel of worship, and something each person must do for himself.
A practice for times of danger only
Not quite. The article says: The kernel of worship, and something each person must do for himself.
The kernel of worship, and something each person must do for himself
Well read. A deeply personal act.
questions.rationale: “Calling upon God or supplication is the kernel of worship… Everyone has to pray for themselves, just as everyone has to perform their own worship.”

questions.article: The Explanation of Meaningfulness of the Universe
questions.q: Everything in nature is found in pairs. What does the article reason from this about human life?
options: Every question has two answers
Not quite. The article says: An imperfect life before death must have its pair – a perfect life after death.
An imperfect life before death must have its pair – a perfect life after death
Yes. Otherwise man alone would be left incomplete.
Every good has an equal evil
Not quite. The article says: An imperfect life before death must have its pair – a perfect life after death.
Every person must marry
Not quite. The article says: An imperfect life before death must have its pair – a perfect life after death.
questions.rationale: “Human life must have a pair, that is, a perfect life after death must be the pair of an imperfect life before death.”

questions.q: A family whose talk had centred on complaints was advised to make their home a “homeschool.” What changed?
options: They moved to another city
Not quite. The article says: Parents and children began learning and reading together, and positive discussion replaced complaint.
Parents and children began learning and reading together, and positive discussion replaced complaint
Correct. Each came to understand his role.
The family stopped speaking at meals
Not quite. The article says: Parents and children began learning and reading together, and positive discussion replaced complaint.
The children were sent away to study
Not quite. The article says: Parents and children began learning and reading together, and positive discussion replaced complaint.
questions.rationale: “Now the atmosphere of negative talk and complaining in their house has become a thing of the past. Instead, topics related to positive thinking and God-realization are being discussed.”

questions.q: What saying does the article quote on why a believer should keep his knowledge up to date?
options: “It is necessary for the believer to be aware of his time”
Right. Including to understand religion in changing times.
“Old knowledge is the safest”
Not quite. The article says: “It is necessary for the believer to be aware of his time”.
“Books are a burden”
Not quite. The article says: “It is necessary for the believer to be aware of his time”.
“Learning is for the young”
Not quite. The article says: “It is necessary for the believer to be aware of his time”.
questions.rationale: “Being aware of the changing times is also important… to understand religion in terms of changing times… It is necessary for the believer to be aware of his time.”

questions.q: The article says submission to God is “not a passive but a positive act.” What does it involve?
options: Withdrawing from society
Not quite. The article says: Actively bringing one’s likes, attitudes and conduct into harmony with God’s will.
Waiting for events to unfold
Not quite. The article says: Actively bringing one’s likes, attitudes and conduct into harmony with God’s will.
Giving up all effort
Not quite. The article says: Actively bringing one’s likes, attitudes and conduct into harmony with God’s will.
Actively bringing one’s likes, attitudes and conduct into harmony with God’s will
Well reasoned. Belief and action together.
questions.rationale: “Submission to God, however, is not a passive but a positive act of bringing one’s likes and dislikes, attitudes and behaviour into harmony with God’s Will.”

questions.q: A villager dug such deep foundations that he had too little material left to roof his house. What does the story illustrate?
options: Deep foundations are always a waste
Not quite. The article says: Failure often comes not from lack of resources but from using them badly.
Failure often comes not from lack of resources but from using them badly
Yes. Planning must match one’s means.
Friends give poor advice
Not quite. The article says: Failure often comes not from lack of resources but from using them badly.
Villagers should not build in brick
Not quite. The article says: Failure often comes not from lack of resources but from using them badly.
questions.rationale: “Failure often results not so much from a lack of resources as from available resources having been under-exploited or wrongly used.”

questions.q: “Success is wholly a thing of the mind.” What two things does the article say bring success?
options: Great wealth and long experience
Not quite. The article says: The determination to reach one’s goal, and the best use of the resources at hand.
Good fortune and influential friends
Not quite. The article says: The determination to reach one’s goal, and the best use of the resources at hand.
Speed and secrecy
Not quite. The article says: The determination to reach one’s goal, and the best use of the resources at hand.
The determination to reach one’s goal, and the best use of the resources at hand
Exactly. Will first, then wise use.
questions.rationale: “Success comes to those who have the determination to achieve their goals and put the resources they have at their disposal to the best possible use.”

questions.q: How does the article describe the stance of a proud person towards truth?
options: He accepts truth only from the learned
Not quite. The article says: Instead of bowing before truth, he wants truth to bow before him.
Instead of bowing before truth, he wants truth to bow before him
Well read. Admitting a fault would lower his status.
He keeps the truth to himself
Not quite. The article says: Instead of bowing before truth, he wants truth to bow before him.
He searches for truth day and night
Not quite. The article says: Instead of bowing before truth, he wants truth to bow before him.
questions.rationale: “Instead of bowing before truth, they want truth to bow before them. Instead of living in harmony with reality, they demand that reality should harmonize with their wishes.”
